uncited: Retrieves the linear indices of the 12 vertex pairs that define the edges of a specific voxel cube in a uniform grid.
It serves as the foundational lookup step for surface extraction algorithms (such as Marching Cubes or FlexiCubes) by mapping topological edge definitions to the grid's spatial data structure.

It differs from its parent [UniformGrid Cell Vertex and Material Retrieval](2999-uniformgrid-cell-vertex-and-material-retrieval.md) by focusing specifically on the 12 edges rather than the 8 corner vertices, providing the connectivity required to determine surface intersections.
It maps edge index $e$ to the local corner indices $c_0$ and $c_1$ within the cube.
Retrieve the first local corner index: $c_0 = \text{CUBE\_EDGES\_FLAT}[2e]$.
Retrieve the second local corner index: $c_1 = \text{CUBE\_EDGES\_FLAT}[2e+1]$.
Retrieve the global linear index of the first vertex: $v_0 = \text{grid.cubes}(\text{cube\_idx}, c_0)$.
Retrieve the global linear index of the second vertex: $v_1 = \text{grid.cubes}(\text{cube\_idx}, c_1)$.
- Time Complexity: $O(1)$ per cube, as it performs a fixed number of 12 lookups.
- Memory Complexity: $O(1)$ auxiliary space for the loop and pair storage.
- When to use: When implementing surface extraction algorithms that require edge-based traversal or triangle generation.
- When not to use: When only vertex positions or material properties are needed without edge connectivity.
Originated in the context of voxel-based surface extraction, specifically within implementations like FlexiCubes.
